analysis.title: The State of AI Financing: A Pause, Not a Pullback
key_insights: September was the second-lowest month of AI-related debt supply this year at about $23bn globally. MS calls the slowdown temporary, driven by front-loaded summer issuance, emerging regulatory and political obstacles to data center construction, and the rates sell-off forcing project-level renegotiations.

AI-related issuance is about $466bn YTD across global credit markets versus $216bn for all of 2025. US IG accounts for $306bn, US HY $53bn, secured leveraged loans $10bn, US securitized $20bn and non-USD corporate credit $75bn.

MS expects 4Q26 supply to slow sequentially but stay above September's pace, with a more moderate cadence than 4Q25. Hyperscalers are expected back in US IG and to keep tapping non-USD markets. Data center paper supply is hard to predict because of urgency to build against sensitivity to higher rates.

In US IG, MS sees the macro backdrop, not supply, as the biggest test through year-end. IG is down 3% in total return YTD and 4% on the quarter, so mutual fund and ETF outflows are expected. There was no AI-related US IG issuance in September, and MS expects at least one more deal.

MS argues rates are rising on strong fundamentals (nominal growth 6%+, earnings growth better). Its economists see AI capex as relatively insensitive to yields and expect high-quality hyperscalers to stay insensitive to higher rates because of visible returns on invested capital and debt being cheaper than equity.
MS's economists' rate path is more dovish than consensus, calling for two more hikes against market pricing closer to four.

Hyperscaler capex estimates are expected to be revised up again at 3Q26 earnings. MS is at about $1.4tn for 2027 combined hyperscaler capex against consensus of about $1-1.1tn. NTM consensus capex expectations are up 8% from last month.

Beyond 4Q26, MS thinks much of the hyperscaler decompression trade has played out. Issuance cadence is more predictable, ROIC estimates are robust, and 2027 capex shifts toward shorter-dated assets such as chips financed through asset-level or private capital, implying a smaller y/y rise in IG issuance than this year.

Hyperscaler credit: HQ hyperscaler spreads are now just 1bp wider than the IG index. YTD widening is 22bp for HQ hyperscalers versus 3bp for the IG index. BBB AI-related names (ORCL, SPCX) trade more than 100bp wider than the HQ cohort.

Off-balance-sheet exposure is rising. Hyperscalers, NVDA and AVGO disclose more than $3.4tn of off-balance-sheet commitments and guarantees. Uncommenced leases total about $1.1tn and purchase commitments about $1.85tn.

Buying CDS protection on hyperscalers remains MS's preferred way to play AI in credit derivatives. The AI CDS basket trades about 45bp wide of CDX IG, liquidity has improved since the March CDX inclusion, and MSFT 5Y is the only name still tighter than CDX IG. Risks are lower issuance than estimated or faster monetization pulling CDS tighter.

MS reiterates preferring collateral-backed risk over unsecured corporate risk. About 30% of AI debt is collateralized. Stabilized ABS/CMBS assets are more insulated from the construction, permit, power and lease-reassignment headlines that drive spread volatility in IG and HY data center paper.

IG data center bonds trade about 120bp wide of the BBB index and 50-200bp behind their tenants' unsecured bonds. MS expects that gap to compress after construction completes and favors deals with high-quality tenants, residual value guarantees, full amortization and rent commencement once shells are delivered.

Reverse Yankee: non-USD hyperscaler supply is $72bn, nearly a third of global hyperscaler supply. Only GOOGL and AMZN have used these markets, across EUR, CAD, GBP, CHF, AUD and JPY, and further EUR deals are reportedly in the pipeline for 4Q. New-issue performance was mixed earlier in the year and more benign since July.

Leveraged finance: AI-related issuance is about $63bn, with HY above $50bn (MS's full-year estimate) and loans above $10bn. AI is about 4% of the HY index, up from 3% in August. September included a record $10bn USD unsecured HY deal. About 70% of AI-related leveraged finance debt is secured or project-finance style.

HY faces rate headwinds. Yields are 8.3% and total returns are near zero, with outflows in four of the past five weeks. HY spreads are 300bp+, the BBB-BB basis went from 50bp to 80bp, and CCCs have widened 400bp this year to 1000bp. MS sees good risk-reward in high-quality HY once rates stabilize.

Data center securitized credit: the 5y Treasury crossed 5%, leaving data center ABS cost of debt more than 100bps higher than at the start of the year. Spreads are leaking wider. MS sees downside risk skew and prefers colocation over hyperscaler data center ABS.

Structural changes in data center securitization: the first floating-rate ABS tranche was issued September 30, a CMBS deal proposed partial amortization, and Vantage priced the lowest-LTV AAA tranche seen so far at about 25%. MS reads these as sponsors crowding in demand as rates rise.

MS cut its ABS/CMBS data center gross issuance forecasts to $25-30bn for 2026 (from $30-35bn) and $40-50bn for 2027 (from about $55bn), and kept $55-65bn for 2028. Total expected through 2028 is $120-145bn.

NVDA credit: MS initiated with a neutral view. The FY2Q27 print showed an expanding support toolkit (shell lease guarantees, revenue-share and price-floor support, potential residual value structures tied to the $500bn partnership). The ~$20bn of future shell leases NVDA plans to reassign raised scrutiny of powered-shell documentation.

ORCL credit: ORCL completed its $20bn equity ATM program in FY1Q27. MS forecasts sizable bond issuance in early CY27 and CY28, sees gross adjusted leverage above 3.5x through FY28, and flags about $65bn of short-dated construction loans funding shells ORCL will lease. The Project Jupiter force majeure notice reported September 24 prompted a response across MS research teams.
MS holds a Buy ORCL 5Y CDS trade (entry +57bp on 9/28/25, now +244bp) and a Sell ORCL 5.2% 2035 and 5.95% 2055 bond trade (entry +167bp and +208bp on 1/23/26, now +212bp and +264bp).

market_movers.rationale: MS Credit initiated NVDA with a neutral view. The balance sheet has become a strategic financing tool, but the 'balance sheet-as-a-service' tail risks are early-stage, opaque and significant.
MS is long CDS protection and short the 2035 and 2055 bonds on funding needs and rising lease liabilities. It sees ratings risk with gross adjusted leverage above 3.5x through FY28.

sector_views.rationale: Macro and outflows are the near-term test rather than AI supply. Hyperscaler decompression is mostly done beyond 4Q26, and credit quality is expected to hold up.
Collateral-backed paper has better risk-reward than unsecured corporates, and stabilized ABS/CMBS assets are more insulated from construction headlines.
Risks skew to the downside as the market absorbs elevated supply through the end of the decade. MS prefers colocation over hyperscaler shells.
Risk-reward looks good once rates stabilize and the issuance calendar is absorbed, while CCCs remain most exposed to higher rates.
Buying protection is the preferred AI expression in credit derivatives given concentration risk and demand for non-economic hedging.

earnings_insights: NVDA FY2Q27 results (already reported): the print expanded the support toolkit to shell lease guarantees, revenue-share and contract price-floor support, and potential residual value structures tied to the announced $500bn partnership. NVDA also disclosed plans to reassign about $20bn of future shell leases. No EPS figures given in this report.

ORCL FY1Q27 (already reported): the company completed its $20bn equity ATM program, lease disclosures imply a roughly 1GW shell lease signing during the quarter, and customer prepays have become a meaningful funding source with limited disclosure. MS looks for clarity on funding, capex and build-out at the October Analyst Day.
3Q26 hyperscaler earnings (upcoming): MS expects another round of upward capex revisions. Its 2027 combined hyperscaler capex estimate is about $1.4tn versus consensus of about $1-1.1tn.

macro_indicators.interpretation: MS says the rate move has a strong fundamental underpinning, so credit quality should hold up.
More dovish than market pricing, which is closer to four hikes. MS sees inflation not falling fast enough alongside robust growth rather than the Fed being behind the curve.
A more hawkish Fed path priced in and a sharp rates sell-off weigh on IG and HY flows and on project-level financing economics.
Above consensus of ~$1-1.1tn, implying higher issuance next year and another leg of upward revisions at 3Q26 earnings.

trade_ideas.description: Buy CDS protection on hyperscalers (AI basket) as the preferred way to play the AI story in credit derivatives
trade_ideas.rationale: Rising AI-related risk concentration in a few names should drive hedging demand, and the AI basket already trades about 45bp wide of CDX IG.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower issuance than estimated, or faster-than-expected monetization improving fundamentals, could tighten CDS spreads back.

trade_ideas.description: Buy ORCLCP 5Y CDS, entered at +57bp on 9/28/25, now +244bp
trade_ideas.rationale: Credit profile deterioration from cash funding needs and rising lease liabilities on new data centers, with lender hedging a possible CDS driver.
trade_ideas.risk: Constructive updates on RPO/growth and financing clarity, term loans playing little funding role, and CDS technicals such as basis selling, construction loan hedge unwinds and profit taking on outright shorts.

trade_ideas.description: Sell ORCL 5.2% 9/26/35 and ORCL 5.95% 9/26/55 bonds, entered at +167bp and +208bp on 1/23/26, now +212bp and +264bp
trade_ideas.rationale: Same credit deterioration thesis, with large media and cable structures considered as relative value comps.
trade_ideas.risk: Additional visibility on long-term monetization and delevering beyond FY28-end, and issuance cadence differing from MS assumptions.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer collateral-backed AI credit over unsecured corporate risk, favoring deals with high-quality tenants, residual value guarantees, full amortization and rent commencement on shell delivery
trade_ideas.rationale: Asset value supports recovery, near-term construction constraints may help asset values, and the spread gap to tenants' unsecured bonds should compress once construction completes.
trade_ideas.risk: Construction delays, permit and power issues, and lease reassignment or contract uncertainty such as the ORCL force majeure episode.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer colocation over hyperscaler data center ABS
trade_ideas.rationale: MS reiterates the preference while expecting data center ABS spreads to keep leaking wider.
trade_ideas.risk: Rising interest rate volatility could hurt data center securitization economics.

risk_factors: Rates sell-off and a more hawkish Fed path triggering IG and HY outflows and project-level renegotiations of data center deals.
Regulatory and political limits on data center construction, plus power and permit delays.
Lease reassignment and contract uncertainty, as in the ORCL Project Jupiter force majeure episode.
Lower-quality issuers and project-level debt are more sensitive to higher rates.
Data center ABS spreads leaking wider as elevated supply is absorbed through the end of the decade.
CCC credits face debt sustainability and refinancing stress, with spreads at 1000bp.
Rising off-balance-sheet leases, purchase commitments and guarantees at hyperscalers, NVDA, AVGO and ORCL.
Opaque, large contingent exposure in NVDA's balance sheet-as-a-service structures and about $1tn of guided GPU/XPU financing still to be absorbed.
ORCL ratings risk, with gross adjusted leverage forecast above 3.5x through FY28-end.

vol_and_positioning: IG is down 3% in total return YTD and 4% QTD, a drawdown level where mutual funds and ETFs could see meaningful redemptions.
HY saw outflows in four of the past five weeks, with total returns approaching negative territory.
Hyperscaler CDS liquidity has improved since inclusion in CDX in the March roll, and weekly volumes continue to increase.
MS expects growing non-economic hedging demand to manage counterparty exposure to a small set of AI names, even if AI investments prove profitable.
The AI CDS basket trades about 45bp wider than CDX IG, and MSFT 5Y CDS is the only hyperscaler still tighter than CDX IG.
The IG data center composite and HY data center composite widened over the last six weeks while data center ABS stayed relatively steady.
geopolitical: Emerging signs of regulatory and political challenges to new data center construction, including power and permit constraints.
Midterm elections cited as a source of near-term volatility alongside rising rates and fund outflows.
Political pushback to build-outs and headline risk around construction delays for lower-rated data center credit.

tension_points.bull_case: Fundamentals are robust: strong returns on AI capex, ROIC estimates holding up, and nominal growth of 6%+. Much of the hyperscaler decompression trade has played out, and the September lull reflects front-loading, not weak demand for capital.
tension_points.bear_case: A sharp rates sell-off, expected IG and HY outflows, political and regulatory limits on data center construction, and spreads leaking wider in data center ABS. Lower-rated and project-level debt is more rate-sensitive.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lower AI issuance than estimated, or faster-than-expected monetization improving fundamentals, which MS says could tighten CDS spreads back and undercut the hyperscaler CDS protection trade.

tension_points.bull_case: ORCL stated the Project Jupiter force majeure notice is a commonplace contractual tool and the project remains on schedule. Customer prepays are a meaningful funding source and RPO/growth updates may be constructive.
tension_points.bear_case: Cash funding needs and rising lease liabilities push gross adjusted leverage above 3.5x through FY28-end. Parent funding may need two large bond deals, with ratings risk and construction loan exposure of about $65bn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Constructive updates on RPO/growth and financing clarity, per the risks MS lists on its ORCL trades. MS looks for that clarity at the October Analyst Day.

tension_points.bull_case: For high-quality HY, risk-reward looks good once rates stabilize, as the issuance calendar is absorbed and earnings growth stays robust.
tension_points.bear_case: HY yields of 8.3%, outflows in four of five weeks, spreads at 300bp+, a wider BBB-BB basis and CCCs at 1000bp, with higher rates worsening debt sustainability and refinancing worries.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rates failing to stabilize, since MS conditions the high-quality HY risk-reward call on rates stabilizing.

theme_stances.key_argument: September's slowdown reflects front-loaded issuance, political and regulatory constraints, and rates, and a busier fall and 4Q are expected as focus shifts to 2027 capex.
theme_stances.evidence: this slowdown is temporary and driven by a combination of significant front-loading

theme_stances.key_argument: Collateral-backed paper has better risk-reward than unsecured corporates, and stabilized ABS/CMBS assets are more insulated from construction headlines.
theme_stances.evidence: We reiterate our preference for collateral-backed risk over unsecured corporate risk.

theme_stances.key_argument: MS expects another leg of upward capex revisions at 3Q26 earnings, with its 2027 estimate well above consensus.
theme_stances.evidence: consensus is still at ~$1-1.1tn for 2027 combined hyperscaler capex
